title: Accomplishments
raw_text:
Accomplishments
Education - Strengthening School Safety
• Chaired the 2013 House Select Committee for School Safety, formed after the 2012 Sandy Hook tragedy, to strengthen school security across Pennsylvania.
• Led bipartisan efforts through public hearings with school officials, law enforcement and parents, delivering a report recommending frequent intruder drills, local safety committees and “choke point” campus designs.
• Co-authored
House Bill 178
, unanimously passed by the House and enacted as
Act 55 of 2017
, requiring annual school security drills for threats like armed intruders. By replacing one monthly fire drill, this law ensures flexibility and preparedness, safeguarding students and staff statewide.
Seniors – Leading During Pandemic Governance - COVID-19
• Directed the House Aging and Older Adult Services Committee, appointed in January 2020, to protect Pennsylvania’s seniors during the COVID-19 pandemic as the first committee to resume work in Harrisburg.
• Brought Health Secretary Rachel Levine before six public hearings in 2020 to demand accountability, challenging the secretary’s unprecedented authority – surpassing even the governor’s – to shut down businesses, schools and places of worship, restricting citizens’ lives.
• Oversaw a March 2021 hearing on vaccination distribution for the state’s most vulnerable seniors and co-authored letters with House Majority Leader Kerry Benninghoff to press for transparency on regulatory suspensions.
• Advanced
House Bills 397
,
398
,
399
and
400
to combat elder abuse, ensuring robust support through programs like prescription drug assistance and the Property Tax and Rent Rebate Program with bipartisan leadership.
HomeOwners - Restructuring Private Road Maintenance
• Authored
House Bill 523
, enacted as
Act 75 of 2021
, to support homeowners by reforming the Private Road Act.
• The law requires property owners to share private road maintenance costs when no agreement exists, addressing banking regulations that blocked federally backed mortgages.
• This reform ensures passable roads and easier home financing, benefiting Pennsylvanians, especially in rural areas.
Reducing Redundant Regulation - Reforming Government for the People
• Championed government efficiency by authoring
House Bills 754
and
755
to streamline bottled water regulation, ensuring better service for Pennsylvania’s citizens.
• Led efforts to consolidate oversight under the Department of Agriculture, reducing duplicative regulations while maintaining safety standards.
• Secured broad bipartisan support in the House, with both bills earning unanimous approval from the House Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee before advancing to the Senate.
• This initiative reflects a commitment to collaborative, common-sense reforms that simplify government processes for businesses and residents,
Appropriations – Budget
• Served on the Pennsylvania House of Representatives Appropriations Committee for six and a half years, playing a pivotal role in scrutinizing and shaping the state's annual budget.
• Participated extensively in budget hearings, rigorously questioning administration officials on spending priorities and accountability for taxpayer dollars.
• Helped determine funding levels and influenced policy across critical areas including education, transportation, public safety, environmental protection, agriculture and economic development.
• Widely regarded as a serious, detail-oriented and reliable legislator who works effectively across the aisle within the chamber to promote responsible spending and fiscal discipline, ensuring efficient use of resources for the benefit of all Pennsylvanians.

title: Coleman, Day to Host Hard-to-Read License Plate Event on Aug. 27
raw_text:
Coleman, Day to Host Hard-to-Read License Plate Event on Aug. 27
August 18, 2026
MACUNGIE — State Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R-16) and state Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) will partner with the Lehigh County Sheriff’s Office, the Pennsylvania State Police and Lower Macungie Township to host a
hard-to-read license plate event on Thursday, Aug. 27, at the Lower Macungie Community Center, 3450 Brookside Dr., Macungie, from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m.
“Assisting with PennDOT issues is one of the most utilized services that my office provides,” Coleman said. “I am pleased to partner with Rep. Gary Day to offer this license plate replacement event to help streamline the process for my constituents.”
“Vehicle owners can have their peeling, fading or unreadable plates inspected on-site and get immediate help filing the paperwork for a free replacement,” said Day. “Replacing damaged plates ensures law enforcement can identify vehicles while saving drivers from costly fines and inspection failures.”
People can sign up for the event at
senatorcoleman.com/events
. Questions about the event or registration can be directed to Day’s office at 610-965-9933 or Coleman’s office at 484-861-4964.
Representative Gary Day
187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Day: More Than $1.34 Million Awarded for School Safety, Mental Health
raw_text:
Day: More Than $1.34 Million Awarded for School Safety, Mental Health
August 14, 2026
HARRISBURG
– - State Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) on Friday announced four school districts serving the 187th Legislative District will be awarded more than $1.34 million in School Safety and Mental Health Grants for physical security enhancements, behavioral health supports or both.
“Students should be able to walk into school each morning knowing the adults around them have the tools needed to keep them safe and help them through difficult times,” Day said. “These grants will allow local school leaders to put resources where they will do the most good, whether that means improving security, expanding mental health support or addressing both priorities.”
The grants are:
•
East Penn School District - $449,924.
•
Northern Lehigh School District - $173,074.
•
Northwestern Lehigh School District - $185,547.
•
Parkland School District - $533,650.
The noncompetitive grant program is administered by the Pennsylvania Commission on Crime and Delinquency. Each school district receives a base allocation of $100,000, plus additional funding calculated using its 2024-25 adjusted average daily membership.
Representative Gary Day
187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

717-772-9845
ccomisac@pahousegop.com

title: Day Invites Local Students to Enter ‘State Representative for a Day’ Essay Contest
raw_text:
Day Invites Local Students to Enter ‘State Representative for a Day’ Essay Contest
August 12, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) is inviting high school students throughout the 187th Legislative District to participate in his “State Representative for a Day” essay contest.
The contest is open to students in grades 9-12. Participants are asked to identify a real-world issue they believe should be addressed by the Pennsylvania House of Representatives and propose a practical solution.
“Young people bring valuable perspectives to the issues facing our communities and Commonwealth,” Day said. “This contest will give students an opportunity to think critically about public policy, develop a realistic solution and learn how ideas can become laws. I look forward to reading their proposals.”
A panel of judges, including Day, will select three winning essays. Each winner will be invited to Harrisburg to shadow Day for a day, tour the state Capitol, and learn more about the legislative process and the responsibilities of a state representative.
Essays must be submitted by Wednesday, Sept. 30, to hbortz@pahousegop.com. Submissions should include the student’s name, grade, school and contact information. Questions about the contest may be directed to Day’s district office at 610-965-9933.
The 187th Legislative District includes the boroughs of Alburtis and Macungie, as well as Heidelberg, Lower Macungie, Lynn, Washington and Weisenberg townships and portions of Upper Macungie Township.

title: Rep. Day: House Bill 1042 Opposition Was Necessary
raw_text:
Rep. Day: House Bill 1042 Opposition Was Necessary
July 27, 2026
HARRISBURG – Following his vote against
House Bill 1042
, Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) issued this statement:
“Although the Pennsylvania Supreme Court’s July 24 deadline has now passed, voting against the revised House Bill 1042 when House Democrats forced a vote on July 23 was necessary. The previous version, which would have earned my wholehearted support, established a clear mandatory minimum sentence for second-degree murder while allowing sentences to reflect an offender’s actual level of participation and culpability.
“Instead of advancing that responsible compromise to the governor, House Democrats replaced it with a last-minute rewrite containing inadequate sentencing provisions, opportunities for forum shopping and unrelated medical-release language with serious loopholes for convicted murderers and sex offenders.
“It is therefore disingenuous to blame those who voted ‘no’ for the missed deadline or claim that their votes endangered public safety. The deadline could have been met by restoring and passing the previous version of House Bill 1042. House Democrats chose instead to force a vote on deeply flawed legislation.
“A looming deadline could not justify abandoning accountability, weakening protections for victims or potentially making it easier for violent offenders to obtain release.”
Representative Gary Day
187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Rep. Day: 2026-27 State Budget Statement
raw_text:
Rep. Day: 2026-27 State Budget Statement
July 14, 2026
HARRISBURG – Following the passage of the 2026-27 state budget, Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) issued the following statement:
“No budget is perfect, but this one reflects the priorities of the people I represent. I’m glad it wasn’t significantly delayed like last year’s budget, which meant people who depend on the budget’s funding weren’t left in limbo for months.
“It boosts PreK-12 education funding by nearly $680 million and ensures every Pennsylvania school district, including those in the 187th District, will see an increase in funding for the coming school year. We’re also preserving the Educational Improvement Tax Credit and Opportunity Scholarship Tax Credit programs, which give families real choices in their children’s education. And it continues necessary support for career and technical education centers by providing an additional $10 million to address waitlists for students interested in pursuing their education at these centers.
“This budget also remembers those who have contributed to our communities. It includes a pension cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for retired municipal police officers and firefighters, many of whom have not received a COLA in more than 20 years. A COLA will also be provided to retired public servants, including teachers, who retired before significant pension changes were implemented in 2001. These are people who dedicated their careers to serving our communities, and it’s long past time they received some relief. There is also increased funding to improve services and strengthen support for our older adults and senior citizens.
“Additionally, this agreement includes $775 million for shovel-ready rural road and bridge projects – $500 million this fiscal year and $275 million next fiscal year – to repair state-owned roads across Pennsylvania beginning this construction season.
“These things matter here at home, whether it’s safer roads, better schools, giving students a path into skilled trades or ensuring our older neighbors are supported wherever they live. This budget shows what’s possible when we prioritize our communities without asking families and businesses to pay more.”
Representative Gary Day
187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Day Announces Grant for Upper Macungie Park Plan
raw_text:
Day Announces Grant for Upper Macungie Park Plan
May 20, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) today announced he helped secure a $90,140 Local Share Account (LSA) grant from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) for the Lone Lane Park Master Plan Project in Upper Macungie Township.
Act 71 of 2004 provides for the distribution of LSA gaming revenues through the CFA to support projects of public interest within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
“Outdoor recreation is hugely popular in the Lehigh Valley, especially during warmer months when families want to get outside and enjoy our parks,” Day said. “Lone Lane Park offers tremendous potential, but its current layout creates real access challenges for many residents. This grant funding will help develop a smart, practical plan to make the park fully accessible so everyone – seniors, families with young children and individuals with disabilities – can enjoy it safely and comfortably.”
The park is the second most used for programming and community events but has accessibility and connectivity limitations. There is only one vehicular access point, no clear pedestrian access points and routes to park amenities are not accessible. The plan will evaluate the park directly and a nearby northern parcel to see if it can be connected to increase park amenities.

187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Day, Coleman Partner to Bring New Community Sign to Heidelberg Township
raw_text:
Day, Coleman Partner to Bring New Community Sign to Heidelberg Township
May 20, 2026
HARRISBURG – Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) and Sen. Jarrett Coleman (R-Lehigh/Bucks) today announced they secured a $43,000 Local Share Account (LSA) grant from the Commonwealth Financing Authority (CFA) to purchase a new outdoor community sign for Heidelberg Township.
Act 71 of 2004 provides for the distribution of LSA gaming revenues through the CFA to support projects of public interest within the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
“Even in this age of social media, important local information can still get missed,” Day said. “This new digital sign at Heidelberg will help ensure our residents – and those just traveling through – stay informed about key community news, events, and public safety updates. It’s a simple, effective way to improve transparency and keep everyone connected”
“I’m proud to join Representative Day in announcing this state grant sought by Heidelberg Township for a new digital sign at the municipal building,” Coleman said. “The township will soon be able to share upcoming event, traffic, safety and other important messages with area residents quickly and efficiently.”
The funding will pay for the purchase and installation of a digital municipal sign that will allow the township to instantly share multiple messages, such as meeting dates, road closures, public safety alerts, volunteer opportunities and community events without delay or limitations of the current manual sign.

187th Legislative District
Pennsylvania House of Representatives

title: Day Announces Grants for 187th District Fire, EMS Companies
raw_text:
Day Announces Grants for 187th District Fire, EMS Companies
February 17, 2026
MACUNGIE – State Rep. Gary Day (R-Lehigh) announced today that six fire and emergency medical services (EMS) companies in the 187th Legislative District were collectively awarded more than $96,000 in funding support through the 2025-26 Pennsylvania Fire Company and Emergency Medical Services Grant Program.
“I am truly grateful for the unwavering dedication and hard work of our first responders. Their service is vital to safeguarding families and communities across the 187th District,” said Day. “This grant program delivers essential funding for smaller projects that support our fire and ambulance personnel. By easing the burden of fundraising, it allows these brave men and women to focus on what they do best: Protect and assist residents in times of need. I am proud to support our first responders and will continue advocating for the resources they need to carry out their life-saving mission.”
Projects eligible for funding include construction or renovation of a fire or ambulance company facility, purchase or repair of equipment, training, recruitment and retention, public education about fire safety, or reduction of existing debt. The funding amounts are contingent on the recipients filing their grant agreements with the Office of the State Fire Commissioner.
The local grants are as follows:
•	Community Fire Company of New Tripoli – $13,000.
•	Fogelsville Volunteer Fire Company – $13,663.17.
•	Goodwill Fire Company No. 1 Inc. – $12,426.48.
•	Lower Macungie Fire Department – $28,136.55.
•	Macungie Ambulance Corps – $15,000.
•	Weisenberg Volunteer Fire Department – $14,075.40.
